architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 mitigates the locally observed 120 C hot-hold viscosity-drift failure mode relative to the E5 high-drift reference while preserving in-support melt behavior.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Primary mitigation is supported if SI15-60 <= 0.305 and SI15-90 <= 0.550, placing both drift windows closer to the E1 low-drift reference than to the E5 high-drift reference, and if the 80-130 C temperature-response check remains monotonic with a documented 120 C state anchor.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fails the mitigation claim if SI15-60 or SI15-90 remains closer to E5 than E1, if low SI is achieved only with impractical or out-of-support viscosity behavior, if process-state shifts are comparable to the claimed improvement without calibration, or if the executed formulation materially changes stoichiometry/process variables outside the candidate definition.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C hold from 15 to 90 min, with predeclared SI15-60 and SI15-90; include 15, 60, and 90 min points at minimum, plus a 120 C initial/state anchor and an in-support 80-130 C temperature-response check.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Full axis coverage and lower modifier burden, but TK100 = 2.5 wt% is below the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% tackifier-like evidence cluster; better treated as a minimum-burden uncertainty probe, not the primary performance-mitigation test.
Full coverage with 17.5 wt% acrylic-like and 5 wt% tackifier-like in a strongly supported region, but higher total modifier burden than needed for the first performance-mitigation experiment.
Strong acrylic-only mechanistic control, but it zeroes the independently supported minor_tackifier_like axis and therefore does not test the full performance-mitigation strategy.
Reactive-core-only baseline control; useful for comparison but does not test the resin-modification mitigation hypothesis.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: Failure mode: the local measured failure is 120 C thermal-hold viscosity drift, with E1 low-drift and E5 high-drift references; therefore the next experiment must measure matched hold-window SI, not infer stability from a static viscosity. Experiment intent: the Planner declared performance_mitigation, so the primary candidate should cover both independently supported intervention axes rather than defaulting to a single-axis causal-control point. Local experiments learned the E1/E5 drift contrast, monotonic in-support temperature response over 80-130 C, and high E2 state/repeatability spread requiring a state anchor. Paper-derived rheological rules contributed the distinction between thermal response, static viscosity, and temporal hold drift, plus the need for state-aware calibration. Curated PUR literature/database priors support a broad acrylic-like modifier region around 15-25 wt% and a minor tackifier-like region centered near about 5 wt% and below about 10 wt%; these priors bound a plausible formulation family but are not direct predictors of the wet-lab outcome. Conservative experimental-design constraints require full axis coverage for performance mitigation, avoidance of exact-analogue-distance optimization, stoichiometry verification, process documentation, and minimum sufficient modifier burden only after sufficiency is established. S1C41 is selected over S1C40 because both are full-coverage candidates at 15 wt% acrylic-like, but S1C41 uses TK100 = 5 wt%, matching the repeated tackifier-like evidence cluster, whereas S1C40's 2.5 wt% TK100 could underdose the supported secondary axis and turn the trial into an ambiguous low-dose probe. This resolves the Skeptic and Robustness-Adjudicator objections by not allowing lower burden to dominate before tackifier-axis sufficiency is established. S1C46 remains a useful robustness follow-up but has a higher total modifier burden. S1C49 is reserved for causal isolation because clean attribution is not a reason to remove a supported secondary modifier from a performance-mitigation experiment.

extrapolation.note: Formulation region is guided by external PUR analogues but the held-out wet-lab result is not predicted; all rheology adjudication remains inside local 80-130 C support.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Canonical bridge from upstream rheological analysis is required before candidate comparison. It should confirm the formulation-only versus state-aware structure, state-shift master-curve implications, temperature-response regularities, and E1/E5 hold-drift contrast using only pre-validation evidence.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After defining the local objective as hot-hold drift mitigation, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 reactive-core anchor, independent acrylic/tackifier axes, and historical/claim boundary before ranking any candidate IDs.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Identify acrylic-like candidate-region priors and distinguish direct numeric formulation anchors from analogue evidence; use them only to bound plausible modifier levels, not to declare an optimum.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Identify minor tackifier/rheology-modifier bounds and processability analogues, especially the conservative below-about-10-wt% guidance, before allowing a multi-axis performance-mitigation candidate.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the low-drift local reference trajectory at 120 C so the candidate objective can compare against measured stability behavior rather than a nominal viscosity target alone.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the high-drift local reference trajectory at 120 C to define the observed failure severity and ensure the next experiment is designed to mitigate the relevant failure mode.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify nominal run spread for the reactive-core anchor before treating any predicted or measured viscosity level as formulation-specific; large state/process variation may require calibration measurements.

action_requests.name: get_temperature_support
action_requests.reason: Confirm the measured temperature support for the E2 reactive-core anchor and choose adjudication temperatures inside the local 80-130 C range, preferably including 120 C to align with hold stability.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Expose the transparent composition summaries for the reactive-core anchor so acrylic-like and tackifier-like modifications can be evaluated without conflating chemistry changes with unknown process-state effects or stoichiometric drift.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Hot-hold stability at 120 C using SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 over the local measured windows, especially 15-60 min and 15-90 min if feasible.
Nominal viscosity level at an in-support anchor temperature, preferably 120 C, with source units preserved and unknown units not invented.
Temperature-response shape over 80-130 C or a reduced in-support sweep sufficient to detect gross processability changes.
State/process repeatability risk, including whether a one-point state calibration is needed before comparing the candidate to E1/E5 references.

Bounded chemistry plausibility: acrylic-like level relative to analogue anchors near 15-25 wt%, tackifier-like level below the conservative 10 wt% upper guidance, and combined-modifier fraction within candidate-space construction rules.
Stoichiometric and reactive-core feasibility relative to the E2 anchor, including whether modifier addition changes NCO/OH balance or dilutes reactive content beyond the intended lattice assumption.
Evidence class: separate directly commensurate local measurements from directional external analogues and from conservative extrapolation limits.
counterfactual_checks: Would the same candidate still be preferred if nominal viscosity level were ignored and only hot-hold SI were considered? If not, the plan may be optimizing the wrong response.
Would the same candidate still be preferred after allowing a state shift consistent with E2 repeatability spread? If not, require stronger calibration or choose a more robust region.
Is the candidate choice supported by independent acrylic-like and tackifier-like evidence, or is a literature percentage being silently converted into an exact local optimum?
Would a single-axis acrylic-only or tackifier-only point be more appropriate if the stated intent were causal isolation rather than performance mitigation?
Does the chosen measurement plan distinguish temperature sensitivity from temporal hot-hold drift, or does it rely only on a temperature sweep?
Does the formulation remain within the pre-result candidate lattice and avoid any information from the blinded validation formulation or outcome?
If the candidate improves SI but worsens repeatability or processability, is the result classified as partially supported rather than supported?
planner.decision_goal: Select one prospective candidate-region experiment that mitigates the locally observed hot-hold viscosity drift while remaining within measured rheology support, bounded candidate-space chemistry, and explicit process-state uncertainty; do not treat the next point as an exact optimum or as a held-out-formulation recovery task.
design_implications: The design objective should penalize hot-hold drift directly, using SI over the measured local window, rather than optimizing only viscosity at one temperature.
The anchor measurement temperature for processability should be 120 C or another point inside the measured 80-130 C support; extrapolated temperatures should not drive selection.

Because process-state shifts and repeatability can be large, the experiment should include at least enough temperature-sweep or one-point state calibration information to separate formulation effect from realization state.

Because the established failure mode is performance drift rather than a single causal question, a bounded multi-component intervention is admissible if acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes are independently supported and the combination remains within the candidate-space bounds.

Directly commensurate numeric anchors are limited: local SI values at 120 C for E1 and E5, and local temperature-sweep support from 80-130 C. External viscosity values near 110-130 C are only broad processability analogues because chemistry, units, and process history differ.

Directional/noncommensurate evidence supports acrylic-family and tackifier-family modifiers as plausible regions for improving PUR hot-melt processability or stability, but it must not be converted into an exact local formulation optimum.

A conservative experimental-design principle is to choose a candidate from the interior of externally supported ranges, avoid exceeding the 30 wt% acrylic-like and 10 wt% tackifier-like lattice bounds, and preserve explicit stoichiometric/process-state checks before execution.
material_regularities_to_use: Temperature sweeps for measured original formulations are monotonic decreasing from 80-130 C and are well described locally by Andrade-like temperature response, so any nominal viscosity comparison should stay inside the measured 80-130 C support.

Thermal response and temporal hot-hold drift are distinct responses: a formulation can have a processable temperature-sweep viscosity yet still fail by viscosity increase during hot holding.

The thermal-hold evidence available pre-result is local and sparse: E1 has SI about 0.095 from 15 to 60 min and 0.168 from 15 to 90 min at 120 C, while E5 has SI about 0.515 from 15 to 60 min and 0.931 from 15 to 90 min at 120 C.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.
